title: Contract Management Software: Evaluation and Implementation Guide
description: Evaluate contract management software for repository structure, clause search, approvals, renewal control, e-signature integration, permissions, and auditability.
author: Emily Nakamura

sections.title: Map the contract lifecycle
sections.body: Document how contracts are requested, drafted, negotiated, approved, signed, stored, renewed, and retired today. Identify who owns each stage, where delays occur, and which contract types create the most risk. Separate legal review from commercial approval and note exceptions for procurement, sales, HR, and finance. This process map becomes the basis for evaluating a platform; without it, teams may automate an unclear workflow and reproduce the same bottlenecks in a new system.

sections.title: Build a usable contract repository
sections.body: Define a consistent taxonomy for contract type, counterparty, business unit, jurisdiction, owner, effective date, renewal date, and status. Test whether the system can find contracts using metadata and full-text search, including scanned files if OCR is needed. Decide how legacy documents, amendments, exhibits, and related agreements will be linked. Validate search results against a representative sample before migrating the full archive, and assign an owner for fixing incomplete or conflicting records.

sections.title: Control templates and clauses
sections.body: Inventory approved templates, fallback clauses, negotiation positions, and language that requires escalation. Check whether legal administrators can maintain a clause library, track versions, and limit which users can change approved text. Test how the system handles non-standard language and whether reviewers can compare revisions clearly. Do not treat automated clause suggestions as legal advice; define the situations where counsel must review the contract and make that escalation path visible.

sections.title: Design approvals and permissions
sections.body: Translate approval policy into explicit rules based on contract value, risk, jurisdiction, data processing, and business unit. Test ordinary renewals, high-value exceptions, non-standard liability clauses, and urgent approvals. Confirm that a requester cannot approve their own request where separation of duties is required. Review role-based access for confidential HR, customer, pricing, and partner agreements, and verify that permission changes and approvals are recorded in an audit trail.

sections.title: Connect signatures and business systems
sections.body: Verify the exact integrations needed for e-signature, CRM, procurement, ERP, identity, and document storage. Test field mapping for counterparty, amount, owner, status, and dates; confirm how amendments and failed syncs are handled. Ask whether the integration is included in the plan or requires a connector or professional services. Define which system is authoritative for each field so a later sync does not silently overwrite the correct value.

sections.title: Manage renewals and obligations
sections.body: Test renewal reminders, notice periods, auto-renewal clauses, termination dates, service-level commitments, and obligations assigned to business owners. A reminder is useful only if the correct date and owner are captured. Create a sample dashboard of upcoming renewals and verify the underlying records manually. Decide how the team records completion, renegotiation, termination, and exceptions, and ensure that missed reminders can be detected rather than disappearing into an inbox.

sections.title: Plan migration and rollout
sections.body: Pilot with a defined set of contract types and include legal, procurement, sales, and finance users. Migrate a small batch first and reconcile document counts, metadata, attachments, and access permissions. Keep the source repository read-only and accessible until acceptance criteria pass. Train users on the request and approval workflow, publish an escalation guide, and assign responsibility for data quality and template maintenance after launch.

sections.title: Measure adoption and control risk
sections.body: Track time from request to signature, approval delays, missing metadata, renewal actions completed on time, search success, and contracts processed outside the system. Establish a baseline before rollout and review the same measures after adoption. Treat cycle time as one metric, not the only goal: faster contracting is not a success if required approvals or controls are bypassed. Reassess templates, permissions, and retention rules when business processes or legal requirements change.
